dedupe_keys.name: foodon farm to fork food ontology obo foundry

description: FoodOn is an open ontology, a shared controlled vocabulary for people and computers, that names foods from farm to fork. It covers the animals, plants and fungi that can serve as food, raw and processed food products, the processes used to make them, and their qualities and ingredients, including generic foods found in processing plants, markets, stores and food distribution points. It belongs to the OBO Foundry family and reuses terms from ontologies such as NCBITaxon, ChEBI and ENVO, so food supply data can be linked with agricultural, environmental and health data. The ontology is free to download as an OWL file under CC BY 4.0, and it is also available to browse in the EBI Ontology Lookup Service, which lists about 40,000 terms in the September 2026 release. The consortium is coordinated from Simon Fraser University, and the reference paper appeared in npj Science of Food in 2018. Coverage is global and multi-cultural, although much of the detail reflects North American and European food traceability needs. Caveats: an ontology, not a dataset of flows or facilities; using it needs OWL tooling or an ontology service. Simulation uses: a common food classification for coupling food supply, trade and food safety models and for tagging data in food system digital twins. Related records: the Global Food Twin data (data-global-food-twin-food-flows) use a coarser set of 82 food groups that could be mapped to FoodOn classes.

name: FoodOn: farm-to-fork food ontology (OBO Foundry)
provider: FoodOn consortium; contact Damion Dooley (Simon Fraser University)
schema_summary: OWL ontology of entities bearing a food role: food sources (animals, plants, fungi), raw and processed food products, processes, qualities and ingredients; imports terms from BFO, ChEBI, ENVO, EO, NCBITaxon, OBI, RO and UBERON; about 40,000 terms in the release loaded by OLS
